outcomes.text: Identify the complement a particular verb and sense allow.
Distinguish an object, a prepositional complement and an optional adjunct.
Preserve the correct verb frame when adding recipients, particles or pronouns.

key_terms.definition: The set of complement patterns available to a word in a particular sense.
A dependent whose type or presence is licensed by the head of its construction.
An added dependent specifying circumstances such as time, place or manner.
A short word such as back or off that forms a construction with a verb and may alternate in position with a noun-phrase object.

options.text: The mixture consists with milk and flour.
options.feedback: In this sense consist selects an of phrase.

options.text: The mixture consists of milk and flour.
options.feedback: In this sense consist selects an of phrase.

options.text: The mixture consists milk and flour.
options.feedback: In this sense consist selects an of phrase.

opening.prompt: Which wording expresses the material that makes up a mixture?

options.text: after lunch
options.feedback: After lunch specifies time. The manual answers what was perused and is the object.

options.text: perused the manual
options.feedback: After lunch specifies time. The manual answers what was perused and is the object.

options.text: the manual
options.feedback: After lunch specifies time. The manual answers what was perused and is the object.

opening.prompt: In “We perused the manual after lunch”, what is the adjunct?

options.text: Explain Jo the result.
options.feedback: Explain takes the result as direct object and licenses a recipient to phrase.

options.text: Explain to Jo to the result.
options.feedback: Explain takes the result as direct object and licenses a recipient to phrase.

options.text: Explain the result to Jo.
options.feedback: Explain takes the result as direct object and licenses a recipient to phrase.

opening.prompt: Which version gives the recipient in the ordinary frame for explain?

options.text: The latch tends that it sticks.
options.feedback: Tend selects a to-infinitival in this construction.

options.text: The latch tends to stick.
options.feedback: Tend selects a to-infinitival in this construction.

options.text: The latch tends sticking.
options.feedback: Tend selects a to-infinitival in this construction.

opening.prompt: Which sentence describes the latch’s tendency?

options.text: It is the finite subject.
options.feedback: Him is accusative, as expected for an ordinary personal-pronoun object.

options.text: It is the object of called.
options.feedback: Him is accusative, as expected for an ordinary personal-pronoun object.

options.text: It is the person who placed the call.
options.feedback: Him is accusative, as expected for an ordinary personal-pronoun object.

opening.prompt: In “She called him”, what makes him the right form?

options.text: She switched it off.
options.feedback: An ordinary unstressed personal pronoun precedes the particle in this construction.

options.text: She switched off they.
options.feedback: An ordinary unstressed personal pronoun precedes the particle in this construction.

options.text: She switched off it.
options.feedback: An ordinary unstressed personal pronoun precedes the particle in this construction.

closing.prompt: How would you replace “the lamp” with “it” in “She switched off the lamp”?

options.text: A ramp was constructed at the café.
options.feedback: Construct does not have the relevant inchoative use. The passive makes a ramp the subject of a complete clause.

options.text: A ramp constructed at the café.
options.feedback: Construct does not have the relevant inchoative use. The passive makes a ramp the subject of a complete clause.

options.text: A ramp destroyed at the café.
options.feedback: Construct does not have the relevant inchoative use. The passive makes a ramp the subject of a complete clause.

closing.prompt: Which ordinary sentence says that a ramp came into existence through the café’s work?

options.text: It changes perused into a preposition.
options.feedback: A time adjunct and the verb’s object perform different jobs.

options.text: It says when, while perused normally calls for what was examined.
options.feedback: A time adjunct and the verb’s object perform different jobs.

options.text: It supplies an object naming the thing examined.
options.feedback: A time adjunct and the verb’s object perform different jobs.

closing.prompt: Why doesn’t “after lunch” provide what perused needs in “We perused after lunch”?

options.text: the manual we came across
options.feedback: The idiomatic combination came across resists fronting across with a relative phrase.

options.text: the manual across which we came
options.feedback: The idiomatic combination came across resists fronting across with a relative phrase.

options.text: the manual we came from
options.feedback: The idiomatic combination came across resists fronting across with a relative phrase.

closing.prompt: Which wording preserves the idiomatic sense “found by chance”?

options.text: Give licenses the double-object frame. Explain uses a to phrase for the recipient in this sense.
options.feedback: The available complement frames are properties of individual verbs and senses.

options.text: Jo must always follow the direct object, regardless of verb.
options.feedback: The available complement frames are properties of individual verbs and senses.

options.text: Explain takes the recipient in the same frame as give.
options.feedback: The available complement frames are properties of individual verbs and senses.

closing.prompt: Why can you say “We gave Jo a copy” but normally “We explained the result to Jo”?
